paras: In February 1888 two hunters found the body of an unidentified, heavily armed man in the Boston Mountains of Arkansas, near a still where a revenue collector had killed its owner the previous fall. No marks showed how he died, but newspapers supposed he was a detective gathering evidence against illicit distilling and headlined the death "Murdered by Moonshiners."

The body lay near the still of a man named Jones, who had been killed there by Revenue Collector Frye the previous fall. The Omaha Bee's correspondent described the region as "filled with moonshiners" and said the many bloody affrays they caused drew no notice unless they were of an extraordinary character.

T. J. Patterson and a companion named McMahon, given as "Kiel" in one version and "Rich" in another, came upon the body while hunting in the Boston mountains. According to a telegram dated Harrison, Ark., February 12, the discovery was made the day before. The dead man was bareheaded, in shirt sleeves and heavily armed, and no one identified him. There were no marks on his person to indicate the cause of death.
The coverage does not report an inquest, an identification of the man, or any arrests.

The story reached the press as a single Harrison dispatch in two forms. The Omaha Daily Bee printed it on February 13 as a special telegram under the headline "Murdered by Moonshiners. Ghastly Find of Two Arkansas Hunters," with closing lines on the lawlessness of the moonshine country. A shorter wire text dated February 13 ran the next day in the Press and Daily Dakotaian at Yankton and the Beatrice Daily Express in Nebraska, both under "Murdered by Moonshiners." Every version treated the man as a likely detective and the moonshiners as the likely killers, though none offered evidence beyond the location of the body.

Only the Bee's telegram went further, supposing that "the moonshiners hanged him and then rut [cut] th[e] body down." The wire version said only that the body was supposed to be a detective's and made no mention of hanging.

bases: An unexplained death: the body of an unidentified armed man was found with no marks showing the cause of death, and only a supposition that moonshiners killed him (A1, A2).
All coverage traces to one Harrison, Ark., dispatch, carried as a special telegram (A1) and as a shorter wire text (A2, reprinted A3); no independent local report was found.
